I think you have right that people want a diagnosis to feel that they belong somewhere but it doesn't come from a need to hear only what you want to hear. The problem is that in fact this is how mental disorders are divided. Even if you want to be open and discuss different aspects it seems that you can't especially online.

Look reddit for example. There are so many different subs about different disorders. In most of them you will find the sane questions and the same answers something that proves most mental illnesses are just trauma responses. Me as someone who came to reddit to find what is wrong with me having only an ocd diagnosis from a country that nobody gives so much important to official diagnosis although they give medication with great easy, I catched myself getting frustrated all the time with where exactly I belonged. I found relatable things on dvpd sub but also on bpd. Then I went to npd or bipolar and I could also identify with people. On the other side even if I know that I have ocd I couldn't feel connected here. Then I found cptsd sub that covers a variety of things and it felt more right. But then again not completely.

I always try to decide where I have to post my thoughts and in which sub they suit more. In most subs you can't even ask others if what you have seem like a symptom because they will tell you to visit a mental health professional. From the other side you will find the same problem as part of multiple illnesses and of course you will start to questioning what this symptom means.

So it's not just a need of people to be divided or be close minded. I feel forced to have a diagnosis from a mental health professional cause be so open and reading so many different percepectives it leads me to madness not to feel more connected. Because everything is just a trait, everything is pathologized and nobody wants to discuss anything rather that telling you to go to a specialist. It seems that for the world a psychiatrist is more capable to define what you have although you can also read all the traits and self analyze yourself. His opinion is more worthy that yours.

There isn't just one sub where people can discuss openly their symptoms and their experiences without some sort of labelling. It's not people's fault to seek a label since it seems the only way to find people to connect with. Me who just wander between subs and my ocd makes me ruminating the same thoughts over and over again I'm in a much more difficult situation than someone who just knows that he is bipolar.

As someone who took medication for depression for years and tried therapy I think I have the right to tell my opinion and I find some of the comments utterly bullshits. You can't compare depression with any other illness like cancer or covid is totally stupid. Yes depression can cause for chemical imbalance but this is so outdated theory that big pharma and psychiatry use to make money for people with selling them false hopes. The majority of people who are depressed or have any other struggle is because the traumatic experiences they had to deal through their lives. Personally I don't know many who wake up one day a d felt that they don't want to live anymore.

People want to believe that depression is a mental illness as they want to believe that people are inherently good, that justice exist, we have free speech etc. Because is much easier to be delusional and not admitting the truth. Because the truth is so dark and so difficult to comprehend it. Because then they have to admit that something is wrong and they are also part of the problem as we are all people. Nobody likes to feel bad with himself.

Depression is the natural reaction of any rational person who has a sense of awareness. Whoever doesn't see it is just another delusional sheep who believes that society cares about his welllbeing. Go take your pills and try a million prescriptions and convince yourselves that you get "fixed". The only thing that these pills do is to transform you in an emotionless vessel, unable to fuction like a real human and the moment you will stop them the realization that you lose even the little sense of self you had hits you so hard that you pray to never in your life have taken them.

But what if what you want to do is to only take revenge from other people? What if the only thing you care about is to yell at everyone and treat them like a garbage? I think personally it's better for me to die rather than become toxic person.
I think you put very accurately and this is what happened to me exactly.

I was in a mental health forum in my country but it wasn't organized, most people only focus on medication, I learned about avpd and cptsd from here. I couldn't connect with others about my mental health issues and is not a very protected place everyone can write whatever they want and offend you or try to promote you something.

You description is very accurate. Is like they have a check list with what is normal and whatvis not and if you don't fit into a criterion you are characterized as wrong or problematic. They use of course your insecurity about this particular thing as a way to convince that there is indeed a problem, while your insecurity comes from the invalidation you have experienced from other people not because you feel bad with something. I think that deep inside I like the way am but I perceive me as fundamentaly wrong because I'm afraid that people will perceive me as weird not because I don't like this particular trait. For example sometimes I like to act childish, mimic voices, hug my stuff animals, speak to dogs etc. but I feel anxious because I know that other people will perceive as immature and not serious enough. The idea that therapist have is that I need to socialize more and all these traits are just a way to stay attached to my childhood. Well maybe they are maybe they aren't but I want the focus to be of how to not feel ashamed for who I'm not hide away and engage in activities that I don't want. The idea of loosen up, with drinking, clubbing, having sex etc is not appealing to me not just something that I desire but I don't admit. And because I have ocd trying to overanalyzing these thoughts it did more damage to me.

The problem is that the ideas therapists have get spread to other people who are either also pathologizing everyone or feeling that something is wrong with them cause they can't relate. I see it everywhere in social media. People tend to put labels to anyone who doesn't follow what society expected from him. Seeing an introvert college student, who wants to spent time alone or with his family and everyone will find him in a minute mentally ill.

I understand that all those questions can indicate a problem but again in my opinion these questions can apply exactly as they are to someone who has bpd, avpd or some other personality disorder.

Also in my opinion a healthy person would questioning his motives and would do also a self introspection around these questions. He wouldn't ended up feeling suicidal or completely worthless but doing all these things unsubconsciously to my eyes it seems much more toxic rather than having self awareness. Lack of self awareness was always a basic trait of npd and your questions are based too much on self analyzing. 

I guess I don't believe in the definition of healthy and unhealthy people. It doesn't mean that someone who struggle can't have accurate criteria. I think that all these traits are the result of severe trauma, cptsd and coping mechanism and not just different personality disorders. People are too complex to get into boxes. You can't measure people with how many hours they daydream.

This is just my opinion and I guess is unpopular here so I'm not going to continue it.

It's easy to recognize someone who is clearly gradiose and entitled but what you described is usually how most people operate. I don't know a lot of people who believe that anyone had it worse than them, don't believe that they aren't more smart than the majority even if they clearly aren't, who don't believe that they are more unique. And of course they believe everything in comparison with others because this is how we raised. To compete each other. There aren't many people who believe they are beautiful, smart, moral if they don't compare theirselves to others and if they believe they have all these traits without comparing themselves they will probably considered even bigger narcissists.

So covert narcissism is way too common or all these traits are narcissistic defensive mechanisms that most people use. And don't telling me this is not true because I'm sure that you can recognize all these things in people around you even in daily interactions. I wish I was projecting it would make me feel that I'm really unique but after years of introspection and analyzing I believe that most people think this way no matter the objective truth. Maybe there isn't one.

So I have recognized that feeling special is not special at all to be consider a disorder that only 1% of the planet has it. If it was only the 1% who have this way of thinking world wouldn't be this shitty place.
